thread:
lee: FYI saw a reproducible onboarding glitch in the sampleapp. When STS tokens rotate rapidly + background paginator is enabled we get a spike of 429s that lasts ~15s.

anya: which SDK and paging strategy?

lee: go-sdk v0.9.1, cursor paging, prefetch window 25, max_inflight=10. STS TTL set to 30s in CI. After each refresh we see a flush of new connections and the server returns 429 for several seconds.

milo: can you share headers or a short trace? wondering if x-client-session flips on token change.

lee: captured headers: x-ratelimit-limit:150, x-ratelimit-remaining:0, x-ratelimit-reset:2630001500, x-client-session:go:session_5c

auth-bot: note: rotating short-lived creds will change token fingerprint unless the client preserves a stable client-id header or connection pool.

anya: common root cause: prefetch resumes immediately after auth update and you get N new requests with new session id so server interprets as many distinct clients hitting per-session quota. two quick mitigations: 1) pause prefetch for a short cool-down after refresh; 2) reuse transport/connection pool to keep session sticky.

lee: tried pause=1s + reuse transport, helped but under heavy concurrency still saw bursts.

milo: also try cancelling in-flight requests during rotate so they don't retry with a new token and pile up. plus add randomized backoff before resuming the prefetch loop.

lee: implemented cancel-on-rotate + randomized resume 200-800ms: severe spikes gone in staging.

devex: let's capture this as a short recipe in the devdocs: "Auth rotation + prefetch: pause, cancel inflight, reuse connection pool, add jittered resume". I'll open a small PR and link it here.

anya: and maybe add a sample snippet for go showing reuse of http.Transport across token swaps.

lee: will add a minimal repro script to the ticket so infra can trace session attribution. uploading now. :thumbsup:
